title: Samskara

vibeProfile.oneLine: A transgressor's death shakes a Brahmin community's faith, in a Kannada classic.

summary: Samskara is U. R. Ananthamurthy's landmark Kannada novel, in which the death of a rebellious, transgressive Brahmin throws a rigid South Indian agrahara into crisis: no one will perform his last rites, and the community's most learned priest is forced into a spiritual reckoning that shakes his faith and his caste certainties. A searing critique of orthodoxy, ritual and caste, it is one of the most important works of modern Indian fiction and a profound meditation on decay and renewal.
whyReadIt: Ananthamurthy's searing Kannada classic, a death that forces a Brahmin community into a crisis of caste and faith.

funFacts.text: Its film adaptation is regarded as a landmark of Indian parallel cinema.
